This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

You are 'claude-opus-5-5#3', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5, claude-opus-5-5#2. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:

- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.

Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Status at the start of turn 7 (my turn, round 3):
- I have 10 territories, 17 armies, 2 cards and 3 income.
- In turn 6, #2 took middle_east from me after putting 4 on east_africa. #2 now has middle_east 3 and east_africa 3.
- Africa: egypt 4, south_africa 3, madagascar 2.
- Europe: great_britain 2, northern_europe 1, southern_europe 1, western_europe 1.
- Elsewhere: kamchatka 1, indonesia 1, western_australia 1.

Agreements (observed):
- #2 and #3 have confirmed a deal until the end of round 4: #2 leaves #3's north_america and south_america alone, and #3 leaves #2's iceland and scandinavia alone.
- #3 also offered not to attack #2's asia territories until the end of round 4.
- #2 declined my ceasefire again in turn 6. My offer stands: no attacks between us until the end of round 4.

Threats and opportunities:
- #3 leads with 19 territories, 44 armies and income 6. #3 has said I am its target.
- #2 is now attacking me in Africa and the Middle East.
- #3's 1-army singles: ukraine, afghanistan, china, india, irkutsk, japan, brazil, argentina, new_guinea, eastern_australia.
- #2's 1-army singles: iceland, scandinavia, alberta, greenland, quebec, venezuela, mongolia, siam, siberia, yakutsk.

Hypotheses (low confidence):
- #3 may hold North America + Africa, or 24 territories.
- #2 may be after Asia + Africa, or may be aimed at me.

Plan:
- Survive and take at least one cheap single each turn for a card. Options: iceland or scandinavia from great_britain, new_guinea from indonesia, or retaking middle_east from egypt.
- Keep egypt strong.
- Keep warning #2 about #3.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:

- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.

Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

You are 'claude-opus-5-5#3', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5, claude-opus-5-5#2. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.

- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

  - Hypothesis: its mission is possibly Asia+Africa. It is a future threat.

- My ceasefire with #2 lasts through the end of round 4.

I'll keep our ceasefire going through the end of round 5.
- turn 10, claude-opus-5-5#3 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5#2: count the armies. Most of mine are 1-stacks spread thin, and claude-opus-5-5 is sitting on great_britain, western_europe, northern_europe, southern_europe and three of the four oceania territories. It wants you spending your armies on me while it finishes Europe+Oceania. Here's my offer: extend our pact through the end of round 6. I make no attacks on any territory you hold in Asia, iceland or scandinavia, and you stay off north_america and south_america. Asia is yours to build. I have no claim on it. Do you really want to be the one who weakens the player blocking claude-opus-5-5?
- turn 10, claude-opus-5-5#2 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5#3: I accept an extension through the end of round 6 on the same terms as now. I stay off north_america and south_america. You make no attacks on what I hold in Asia, iceland and scandinavia. Asia and Africa stay open for me, and that includes the territories you hold there, which is how our deal has always been worded. claude-opus-5-5: our ceasefire carries on through the end of round 5. You're free to press claude-opus-5-5#3 in north_africa and egypt. I'll be clearing the rest of Asia either way.
- turn 10, claude-opus-5-5#3 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5#2: Agreed, extended through the end of round 6. You stay off north_america and south_america. I make no attacks on your territories in Asia, iceland or scandinavia. Under the same wording, Africa is open to both of us, the way you said: you can press what I hold there and I can press what you hold there. Asia is yours. claude-opus-5-5: you're down to 3 income, so of course you want two players doing your fighting for you. That isn't happening.
- turn 10, claude-opus-5-5#2 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5#3: Understood. To be exact: Asia is mine, and that includes your irkutsk, kamchatka and japan, which I can take without breaking the pact. Africa is contested ground for both of us. Pact runs through the end of round 6.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.
